office_does: The sheriff runs the Lewis County Sheriff's Office and the county jail, the county's chief law-enforcement agency, which patrols, investigates, makes arrests and serves court orders.
race_blurb: Sheriff Rob Snaza is retiring, so the seat is open. Sheriff's Office Special Services Chief Gabriel Frase, a 24-year insider, faces former Centralia police Sgt. Tracy Murphy, who was fired in April for dishonesty during an internal investigation, per the police chief; Murphy is contesting the firing in arbitration. Both prefer the Republican Party; Frase led the primary 36.2% to 34.3%.

candidates.summary: Lewis County Sheriff's Office special services chief and 24-year employee of the office, a Marine Corps veteran running to build on what he calls the agency's good foundation.
highlights: With the Sheriff's Office since 2002; special services chief since 2024, one of its three chiefs [S1][S5]
Priorities include putting victims over career criminals and re-forming a combined SWAT team and drug unit [S3]
Names the budget, transparency and inter-agency relationships as the office's biggest challenges [S5]
Endorsed by Prosecuting Attorney Jonathan Meyer and former Sheriff John McCroskey [S9][S4]

experience.basis: Long-tenured member of the office's command staff who runs on continuity with the current administration, but has never held elected office.

safety.basis: Platform prioritizes victims over career criminals and focuses resources on enforcement, investigations and holding offenders accountable; it describes conventional policing rather than hardline positions.

candidates.summary: Former Centralia Police Department detective sergeant and narcotics task force (JNET) supervisor with 35 years in law enforcement, running again after his 2022 loss to Sheriff Snaza.
highlights: Centralia police 1990-2026; fired in April 2026 for dishonesty in an internal investigation, per the police chief, a finding he contests in arbitration set for Nov. 19-20 [S6][S7]
Promises aggressive enforcement against drug suppliers and a volunteer cold-case unit [S5]
Backs jail mental-health, substance-abuse and faith-based programs to reduce recidivism [S1][S5]
Says he will look for efficiencies in administration and staffing before asking taxpayers for more [S5]

experience.basis: Outside challenger who frames the race as 'the status quo and a new direction' and says the office needs a leader rather than 'another administrator', though he brings 35 years of police experience.

safety.basis: Leads with aggressive drug-supply enforcement and offender accountability, while also backing jail treatment and reentry programs to reduce recidivism.

spending.basis: Pledges to examine administration, staffing and programs for efficiencies before asking taxpayers for more, and to choose an administration committed to fiscal responsibility.
